questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Negated Sentence in Symbolic Form
questions.problem:
$\sqrt{2}$ is **not** an integer or rational number.

Express the compound statement above in symbolic form given the following:

- $P:\sqrt{2}\text{ is an integer number}$

- $Q:\sqrt{2}\text{ is a rational number}$
questions.worked_solution:
The given sentence is the negation of the following sentence: 

$\sqrt{2}$ is an integer or rational number, 

which can be expressed symbolically as $P∨Q.$

The negation is represented by the symbol "$¬$". 

Therefore, the given sentence is expressed symbolically as $¬(P∨Q).$

questions.worked_solution:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So, we can simplify $¬(¬P)$ to $P.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to 

$$
P∧Q.
$$

Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So, we can simplify $¬(¬D)$ to $D.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to 

$$
¬C∧D.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Completing a Truth Table for a Compound Statement
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for $P∨Q.$ Remember that $P∨Q$ is true if either $P$ is true or $Q$ is true.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Finally, we add a column for $¬(P∨Q),$ where the truth values are opposite to the corresponding values in the column for $P∨Q.$

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

questions.knowledge_point: Completing a Truth Table for a Compound Statement
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∧¬Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for $¬Q,$ where the truth values are opposite to the corresponding values in the column for $Q.$ 

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Then, we add a column for $P∧¬Q.$ Remember that $P∧¬Q$ is true if both $P$ and $¬Q$ are true. 

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Finally, we add a column for $¬(P∧¬Q).$ Remember that the truth values of $¬(P∧¬Q)$ are opposite those of $P∧¬Q.$ 

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∧¬Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
